dedupe_keys.name: california strawberries stochastic hub and spoke optimisation of a cold food supply chain under climate driven yield uncertainty

description: This case study plans distribution routes for a produce cold supply chain while accounting for the effect of climate variability on crop yields. David Hernandez-Cuellar and Krystel K. Castillo-Villar of the University of Texas at San Antonio and Fernando Rey Castillo-Villar of Universidad Panamericana in Mexico published it in the journal Foods in 2025. They built a stochastic hub-and-spoke network optimisation model that minimises transport costs by choosing distribution routes, and applied it to strawberries in California, the leading US producing state, with several weather scenarios based on climate models and real soil data. Most earlier models of this kind are deterministic and ignore yield uncertainty, which rises with carbon dioxide, shifting temperatures and extreme weather and can force distributors to change suppliers at extra cost. The article is available online, free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is California production regions and their distribution network. Caveats: the case covers one crop, and yield scenarios depend on the climate and crop models chosen. Simulation uses: a stochastic network design approach and scenario setup for climate-aware food distribution and cold chain resilience models. Related records: FoodFlows county food flows, including cold chain flows (data-foodflows-us-county-food-flows), describe US food movements at national scale.
